hpi: {{patient_name}} presents with rash, lymphadenopathy, and possible genital lesion history. Secondary syphilis: diffuse maculopapular rash (INCLUDING palms and soles — key differentiating feature), condyloma lata (wart-like lesions in moist areas), lymphadenopathy, flu-like symptoms. Primary syphilis: painless indurated chancre at inoculation site (resolves spontaneously). Caused by Treponema pallidum (spirochete). Diagnosis: screening with RPR or VDRL (non-treponemal — titer correlates with disease activity). Confirm with treponemal-specific test (FTA-ABS, TP-PA). Darkfield microscopy of chancre fluid can directly visualize spirochetes. HIV testing (high co-infection). Treatment: benzathine penicillin G 2.4M units IM once (primary/secondary/early latent). Doxycycline if penicillin-allergic. Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction may occur (fever, myalgias, headache within 24h). Report to public health. Partner notification. Follow RPR titers to confirm cure (4-fold decline).
